plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.includedUsage: None; every resource bills at list rates.
plans.quote: No plans and no tiers, and nothing charged per Sprite. Metered per hour of active use.
plans.limitsQuote: Sprite creation rate is also tiered: 10 sprites/minute on pay-as-you-go, rising with plan tier from 60/minute on Adventurer up to 240/minute on Mythic.
plans.notes: The same pricing page also says there are no tiers, while the product FAQ on fly.io/sprites sells tiers and the FAQ quotes a per-org concurrency ceiling. 10 creates/minute on pay-as-you-go comes from the FAQ.

plans.name: Hero
plans.includedUsage: 1,200 CPU-hours, 4,800 RAM GB-hours and 150 GB of storage per month; usage above the allowance bills at standard rates on top of the fee.
plans.quote: Example: Hero ($100/mo) includes 1,200 CPU-hours, 4,800 RAM GB-hours, and 150 GB of storage
plans.limitsQuote: Hero allows 100 concurrently running sprites and 100 warm sprites; cold sprites are unlimited, and higher tiers raise those ceilings.
plans.notes: The pricing page says no plans exist; Hero is the only tier whose fee and full allowance are quoted on a live Fly page.

plans.name: Mythic
plans.includedUsage: 28,000 RAM GB-hours included (the FAQ quotes only the RAM bucket); overage at standard rates.
plans.quote: One customer's usage was close to Mythic's 28,000 included RAM GB-hours, but at $2,000/mo the plan cost more than the overage it saved.
plans.limitsQuote: Sprite creation rate is also tiered: 10 sprites/minute on pay-as-you-go, rising with plan tier from 60/minute on Adventurer up to 240/minute on Mythic.
plans.notes: 240 creates/minute on Mythic comes from the same FAQ paragraph as the creation-rate quote.

plans.name: Adventurer, Veteran, Champion, Legend, Epic
plans.quote: Pay-as-you-go and the plans below Hero (Adventurer, Veteran) have community support.
plans.limitsQuote: Hero, Champion, and Legend include Standard email support; Epic and Mythic include Premium.
plans.rateQuote: Sprite creation rate is also tiered: 10 sprites/minute on pay-as-you-go, rising with plan tier from 60/minute on Adventurer up to 240/minute on Mythic.
plans.notes: These five tiers are named on the live FAQ but their fees and allowances are not published there. 60 creates/minute on Adventurer is the only published limit. Battleships carries a full ladder attributed to a 2026-01-16 community post; see diffs.

compute.billingBasis: Per-resource usage: cumulative CPU time, actual memory time and storage. One fixed Sprite shape; memory is autoscaled rather than chosen.

increment.quote: All compute resources are billed per second. Storage is billed hourly but aggregated monthly.
increment.conflict: The pricing page says 'Metered per hour of active use' and 'All resources are billed hourly, based on actual usage.' Treat per-second as the finer, more specific statement and confirm with Fly for invoicing.

perResourceRates.quote: Cumulative CPU usage measured by cpu.stat

fixedSizes.name: Sprite
fixedSizes.quote: The vCPU count and the storage ceiling are fixed; memory is handled automatically.
fixedSizes.ramQuote: up to 8 CPUs and 16GB of RAM for any given run
fixedSizes.notes: No fixed hourly or monthly price: the bill is usage-based. Memory is platform-managed, advertised up to 16 GB per run.

compute.planRates: Plan fees buy non-fungible buckets of CPU-hours, RAM GB-hours and storage GB; overage bills at the same list rates as pay-as-you-go.
compute.notes: Do not substitute Fly Machines preset prices: Sprites have their own section on the pricing page. The FAQ says plans' allowances are not unlimited usage.

hot.quote: Hot Bills while the Sprite is awake

cold.quote: Cold Bills for as long as you keep it

disk.capacityQuote: Every Sprite starts with 100 GB of storage.
disk.billedOn: bytes actually written, not the 100 GB ceiling
disk.writtenQuote: you pay for the bytes you actually write, not the full 100 GB

billedWhileStopped.quote: CPU, memory and hot storage bill while a Sprite is awake. Cold storage bills until you delete the data.

snapshotStorage.pricingModel: Checkpoint blocks are billed as stored blocks at the storage rates; no separate checkpoint rate is published.
snapshotStorage.quote: You're billed for the blocks actually kept, and deleting a checkpoint frees that space right away.

retention.stoppedDataKept: Indefinitely, at the cold storage rate, until the Sprite or its data is deleted.
retention.quote: All data is permanently deleted: files, packages, checkpoints. No undo.
retention.notes: Warm and cold states both stop compute billing; cold storage continues. There is no published retention limit or expiry for a Sprite that still exists.

storage.notes: The FAQ's shorthand that warm and cold are 'not billed' means no compute charge; the pricing page separately bills cold storage for as long as the data is kept.

egress.quote: No. Sprites bandwidth isn't metered today.
egress.notes: The FAQ adds that any egress lines on an invoice come from Fly Machines, not Sprites.

other.notes: That $2.00/mo line is under Machines Storage and network. No Sprites-specific IPv4 price or allocation is published; Sprites are reached on their own HTTPS URL.
No per-user or per-seat charge is published; plan limits are per organization.

other.quote: Billed hourly, with nothing to pick up front

freeTier.limits: One $30 credit per user and at most one per organization; it applies to Sprites usage only and cannot pay a plan fee.
freeTier.quote: Each user can grant one $30 trial credit, and each org can receive at most one.
freeTier.quote2: Credits apply to Sprites usage only. The monthly subscription fee is billed separately and isn't covered.
freeTier.notes: Not a recurring free tier. The product page markets it as 'Create, like, 500 Sprites free.'

diffs.quote: No plans and no tiers, and nothing charged per Sprite.

teams-accounts.title: CLI Authentication (Fly.io account and org switching)

manualRoute: Install the Sprites CLI and sign in with a Fly.io account, then create a Sprite (sprite create).
Install the agent inside the Sprite, either over sprite console or by pointing the agent's terminal backend at Sprites.
Register the agent as a Sprite service so the runtime restarts it after a cold wake, and give it an HTTP port if it needs to answer requests.
Keep it awake during long runs with the Tasks API; otherwise it pauses about 30 seconds after activity stops.

evidence.claim: Fly's own FAQ markets Hermes and OpenClaw as things to run on a Sprite.
evidence.quote: Hermes, Pi, OpenClaw… whatever your flavour, an agent with access to your inbox and calendar shouldn't live on your laptop. Give it a Sprite that sleeps until it's needed and wakes up remembering everything.

evidence.claim: But the only official Hermes integration is a terminal backend: Hermes keeps running on your own machine and only its shell commands run in Sprites. That is not hosting Hermes on Sprites.
evidence.quote: adds a terminal backend. Hermes stays on its existing host, while its shell commands execute in persistent Sprites.

evidence.claim: A service is the supported way to bring an agent back after a cold wake.
evidence.quote: A service is a process the Sprite runtime owns: it starts when the Sprite boots, restarts if it crashes, and can receive the HTTP traffic that hits your Sprite's URL.

evidence.claim: Getting started is a command-line flow, not a dashboard flow.

deploy.notes: No official Hermes or OpenClaw hosting template or one-click deploy was found. A non-coder cannot install and supervise the agent from the dashboard alone; the documented path is CLI plus shell. An always-on agent also has to defeat the ~30 second idle pause with a service or the Tasks API, and a task hold is capped at 1 hour and must be renewed.
